hn-50341174.t: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
hn-50341174.s: We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms.
ex: We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. This might be a big deal for both optimization and interpretability. Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x. All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops.

hn-50339494.t: Anthropic's internal AI use, at retail prices, now exceeds its employee pay
hn-50339494.s: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals a striking milestone: Its internal AI usage is now valued above employee compensation.
ex: Here's a remarkable milestone in the AI revolution: Anthropic now spends more on internal AI usage than it does paying employees. The company revealed this in its IPO filing. In April, the value of Claude AI used internally, calculated at prices Anthropic charges customers, exceeded its monthly employee compensation costs, excluding stock awards. There's an important distinction here. Anthropic isn't actually spending more cash on AI than salaries. It's valuing its internal AI consumption at retail prices. Still, this feels like a watershed moment for the tech industry. In March, I wrote about a new trend: Tech companies are starting to treat AI tokens (the main way to measure usage) as a fourth component of employee compensation, alongside salary, bonuses, and stock awards. Anthropic's numbers show why. More than 90% of the code added to its software in September was written by Claude. Meanwhile, revenue has grown vastly faster than headcount.

hn-50337439.t: Anthropic reports $17B in Q3 revenue, commitments of $895B in revised S-1
hn-50337439.s: Anthropic unveiled its S-1 prospectus last week, but the initial filing only included the company's financials through the first half of the year.
ex: Anthropic reported updated financials as part of an amended Form S-1 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday, giving investors a more comprehensive look into the state of its business. The artificial intelligence company said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic had a loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. Anthropic unveiled its highly anticipated prospectus last week, bringing the company one step closer to a potentially historic initial public offering. The initial filing only included the Claude maker's financials through the first half of the year. During its third quarter, Anthropic generated roughly $17 billion in revenue, up about 1,127% from the same period last year.

hn-50341462.t: Ubuntu still has not released patch for Linux 0day RCE in almost 3 weeks
hn-50341462.s: No patched kernels are available yet for 22.04, 24.04, or 26.04 despite a CVSS 9.8 rating.
ex: No patched kernels are available yet for 22.04, 24.04, or 26.04 despite a CVSS 9.8 rating. Ubuntu has not shipped fixed kernels for CVE-2026-98432, a critical vulnerability scored CVSS 9.8, leaving the 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS releases without a vendor update. Operators running those releases therefore have no official kernel package that closes the hole. The gap matters most for internet-facing and multi-tenant self-hosted systems that rely on Ubuntu’s LTS kernels for isolation and privilege boundaries; until packages appear, those hosts remain exposed to whatever remote or local attack the CVE enables. Ubuntu has not announced an ETA for the fixes. In the interim, affected administrators are left to decide whether to stay on the stock kernel, apply out-of-tree mitigations if any exist, or move workloads onto releases or kernels that already carry the patch.

hn-50336138.t: Last night an AI agent performed brain surgery on a mouse
hn-50336138.s: Last night an AI agent performed brain surgery on a mouse. We gave it 19 gene therapy vectors in a spreadsheet, a mouse model of epilepsy, access to a motorize surgery rig with cameras and one goal…
ex: Post Log in Sign up Post Log in Sign up Gabriel Ocana-Santero on X: "Last night an AI agent performed brain surgery on a mouse. We gave it 19 gene therapy vectors in a spreadsheet, a mouse model of epilepsy, access to a motorize surgery rig with cameras and one goal: reduce seizures. It picked the drug. It picked the brain region. It derived the coordinates from three papers. Then it drove the stereotaxic arms into the brain and injected 250 nanolitres while watching the entry site through the rig camera for bleeding. A licensed vet gated every irreversible step and held a physical kill switch to stop the AI agent. Thread on what it decided, what it saw, and the moment it refused to let me override it.

hn-50334704.t: I've updated my Linux System Call website and API
hn-50334704.s: The Linux syscall table for 27 architectures: every system call number, argument and register, with a table per architecture, from Linux 3.3 to 7.3.
ex: Every Linux syscall table in one place, grouped by architecture: system calls for 27 architectures with their numbers, arguments and registers, from Linux 3.3 to 7.3. Every architecture's table, with the full history of when each syscall appeared and when it was dropped, is also a plain JSON file at / /syscalls.json, for example /x64/syscalls.json. Number in NR, arguments in ARG0 to ARG5, then the instruction. The result comes back in RETURN. Any kernel release, diffs between releases and more in the API docs. Entries get added and, rarely, removed between releases. Each architecture page has a kernel selector, and its JSON download records when each entry first appeared (since) and when it was dropped (removed_in). Removed entries stay visible: pick "all, with removed" in the kernel selector and each dropped syscall is marked with the release that dropped it. Everything on this site is read from the kernel source itself.

hn-50330456.t: AI delivers 'zero financial payoff' to most companies, Apollo economist says
hn-50330456.s: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."
ex: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants?

hn-50342284.t: Oracle files to sell $20B in new stock, bonds to finance AI buildout
hn-50342284.s: Oracle filed plans on Monday to issue new shares and more debt to finance its artificial intelligence buildout.
ex: Oracle filed plans on Monday to issue new stock and more debt to finance its artificial intelligence buildout. The hyperscaler will sell $10 billion in common stock and $10 billion in senior notes, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. While the fundraising was already outlined at an investor day last week, shares tumbled 8.8% Monday. "This seems to be exactly what they previewed," said Rob Oliver, senior research analyst at Baird. "So I'm not sure why the market is freaking about it." Oracle said it plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, which may include capital expenditures, repayments of debt and future investments. The hyperscaler's stock initially bounced after last Wednesday's investor day, when Oracle also issued a revenue forecast of at least $225 billion for fiscal 2030. At the time Oracle also said it was limiting its additional capital market funding for the fiscal 2027 to 2030 investment cycle to that $20 billion.

hn-50330253.t: So I guess everyone uses LLMs to think now
hn-50330253.s: so i guess everyone uses llms to think now
ex: my thoughts on the current state of llms in development and security in recent times i've been asked a lot the question of "what ai model did you find to use this?", practically for all of the articles on this blog. the answer has always been my brain, i have never used ai for any kind of research i published, ever. the next question is often why, followed up with "you would be so unstoppable with claude mythos" this article should explain why i don't like using ai for my research, and my general opinions on llms in both development and cybersecurity it's as simple as i do this for fun, and i don't find giving an ai all the fun at poking at something instead of doing it myself fun. put it another way, i like using my brain i like coding, i like staring at devtools, binary ninja, or whatever else for hours, i like exploring weird library source code and tracing it with nothing but github code search and a dream, it is fun to me.

hn-50340088.t: Subvocal – Talk to your computer without making noise
hn-50340088.s: Hi HN, we're Aarush and Arnav from The Subvocal Company (YC F26) ( https://subvocal.company/ ). We’re building smart glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud.
ex: Hi HN, we're Aarush and Arnav from The Subvocal Company (YC F26) ( https://subvocal.company/ ). We’re building smart glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud. You can mouth words silently and discreetly and the glasses decode them to text at the speed of speech. Here's a video of Dave from YC trying it out: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9QdX1eObVYI (Edit: you don't actually have to move your lips or even open your mouth for this to work! Since the RF can see inside your mouth the system can be fine tuned on "internal speech". This isn't the automatic tongue movements that occur when "thinking" words to yourself, but more like mouthing with your lips closed. It's a bit weird to do, but with practice, we have been able to get it down pretty well.) Arnav and I were studying CS at Georgia Tech at the beginning of the year, with no experience in silent speech or sensing. We were both AI-native builders and power users of Wispr Flow.

hn-50337608.s: In case you missed it: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) bug in the Linux kernel's TCP code. It's been there since 2016, so virtually every Linux server on the planet has it, and it can be hit…
ex: In case you missed it: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) bug in the Linux kernel's TCP code. It's been there since 2016, so virtually every Linux server on the planet has it, and it can be hit remotely. Anthropic says it built a working exploit that gets root on a server. A total takeover. Debian patched it on October 16. Ubuntu still doesn't have a patch more than two weeks later. Every supported release, LTS included, is listed as "Vulnerable". Ubuntu's website promises "timely patches for critical vulnerabilities." Ubuntu hasn't shipped the patch nine days after it was rated 9.8 and six days after a working root exploit. Very fucking timely indeed. Software is full of this blabber where words mean nothing. Ubuntu uses words like these: "Timely." "Enterprise-grade." "Production grade." "Enterprise resilience. Developer velocity. Build with confidence on Ubuntu." Somebody, or perhaps worse, some special team at Canonical is dedicated to writing these........

hn-50335615.t: Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
hn-50335615.s: Chains in seven countries say cooling unit temperatures rose overnight in incident similar to hack of French stores
ex: Chains in seven countries say cooling unit temperatures rose overnight in incident similar to hack of French shops Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries have said the temperatures of refrigerators and freezers in some of their shops soared overnight to as high as 50C (122F), echoing a cyber-attack last month that caused millions of euros of damage in France. Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday, and several companies confirmed they had been hacked. The EU food and agriculture commissioner, Christophe Hansen, said the repeated cyber-attacks were deeply concerning, calling them “a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers’ confidence in it”.

hn-50344181.t: BYD sold more EVs last month than the US did all quarter
hn-50344181.s: BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.
ex: BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter. The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026. BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark. To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates. October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year. BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month.

hn-50339221.t: Warsaw in voxels – An interactive 3D map of the city centre
hn-50339221.s: Central Warsaw in 1 m voxels, built from OpenStreetMap, LiDAR and the city's tree database. Walk around the Palace of Culture, change the date, hour and weather, or possess a pedestrian.
ex: Explore central Warsaw in voxels - slightly inspired by Minecraft, and MagicaVoxel. You can change the date, time of day and weather, explore the city, or click on a pedestrian to control them (here a bit of inspiration from Dungeon Keeper). Works best on desktop, but I tried to make it usable on mobile too. The initial load can take a while. It's based on several open datasets, including: - OpenStreetMap ( https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=6/52.02/19.14 ) - buildings, streets, sidewalks, tram tracks, etc - GUGiK / Geoportal ( https://www.geoportal.gov.pl/ ) - LiDAR for building heights and trees, aerial imagery for colours - Warsaw's city tree database ( https://mapa.um.warszawa.pl/ ) - individual tree species, used for seasonal foliage Open-source ( https://github.com/stared/warsaw-vibe-voxel ), so feel invited to (re)use it as you wish!

gh-1441555426.s: ChatGPT-style generative UI for Open WebUI: photo galleries, live maps with real routes, multi-day trips, budgets, calculators, live weather & stocks, link previews, and one-click…
ex: ChatGPT-style generative UI for Open WebUI — real photos, live street maps with routes, place cards, itineraries, charts and follow-ups, rendered right inside the chat. Open WebUI answers in markdown. ChatGPT answers with an interface: photos of the places it mentions, a map with the route, cards you can scroll, and next questions you can tap. Frontier UI brings that to any model in Open WebUI. The model writes one small JSON spec. The tool does the rest on the server — finds real photos, verifies places on the map and draws real street routes — then renders a polished, theme-aware card inline in the conversation. 1. Workspace → Tools → + in Open WebUI, paste frontierui.py and save. 2. Workspace → Models → your model → Tools: enable Frontier UI. Turn off other generative-UI tools so the model has one clear choice. Native function calling works best. 3.
